title: bc.b
---
## Broadcasted Boolean Operations {.unnumbered}


### Description

The <code>bc.b()</code> function
performs broadcasted logical (or Boolean) operations on 2 arrays. <br />
<br />
Please note that these operations will treat the input as <code>logical</code>. <br />
Therefore, something like <code>bc.b(1, 2, "==")</code> returns <code>TRUE</code>,
because both <code>1</code> and <code>2</code> are <code>TRUE</code> when treated as <code>logical</code>. <br />
<br />
For regular relational operators, see [bc.rel](bc.rel.qmd). <br /> <br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>bc.b(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.b(x, y, op)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code>, <code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
conformable arrays of type <code>logical</code>, <code>numeric</code>, or <code>raw</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="op">op</code></td>
<td>
a single string, giving the operator. <br />
Supported Boolean  operators: &amp;, |, xor, nand, ==, !=, &lt;, &gt;, &lt;=, &gt;=.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
further arguments passed to or from methods. <br /> <br />
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<code>bc.b()</code> efficiently casts the input to logical. <br />
Since the input is treated as logical, the following equalities hold for <code>bc.b()</code>:


<ul>
<li> &quot;==&quot; is equivalent to <code>(x &amp; y) | (!x &amp; !y)</code>, but faster;

</li>
<li> &quot;!=&quot; is equivalent to <code>xor(x, y)</code>;

</li>
<li> &quot;&lt;&quot; is equivalent to <code>(!x &amp; y)</code>, but faster;

</li>
<li> &quot;&gt;&quot; is equivalent to <code>(x &amp; !y)</code>, but faster;

</li>
<li> &quot;&lt;=&quot; is equivalent to <code>(!x &amp; y) | (y == x)</code>, but faster;

</li>
<li> &quot;&gt;=&quot; is equivalent to <code>(x &amp; !y) | (y == x)</code>, but faster. <br /> <br />

</li></ul>



### Value

A logical array as a result of the broadcasted Boolean operation. <br /> <br />



### See Also

[broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd) <br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")

x.dim <- c(4:2)
x.len <- prod(x.dim)
x.data <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), x.len, TRUE)
x <- array(x.data, x.dim)
y <- array(1:50, c(4,1,1))

bc.b(x, y, "&")
bc.b(x, y, "|")
bc.b(x, y, "xor")
bc.b(x, y, "nand")
bc.b(x, y, "==")
bc.b(x, y, "!=")



```
